title.en: Chief Minister, Council of Ministers and the State Legislature
The real head of the state

text.en: In a state, the Governor is the nominal head, but the Chief Minister is the real executive. He leads a Council of Ministers that answers to the Legislative Assembly, the house the people elect.

The Governor is the head of the state, and the Chief Minister is the head of the government.
The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor under Article 164(1), usually the leader of the majority party in the Legislative Assembly.
His term is not fixed: he stays as long as he enjoys the support of the majority of the Assembly.
Article 163 provides a Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at its head to aid and advise the Governor.
The Council is collectively responsible to the Legislature, and a non-member minister must win a seat within six months.
The total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, cannot exceed fifteen percent of the Assembly's strength.
The Chief Minister recommends ministers, allocates portfolios, shuffles the ministry, presides over the Council and coordinates ministers.
He advises the Governor on summoning and proroguing the legislature, announces policy on the floor, and may recommend dissolution.
The Council formulates state policy, controls financial policy, finalises the Budget, and decides the legislative programme.
The Cabinet, only the cabinet ministers, is the real centre of authority, and works through standing and ad hoc committees.
Most states have a unicameral legislature, but Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana have a Legislative Council also.
The Legislative Assembly is directly elected by adult franchise, has between 60 and 500 members, and has a five-year term, though it can be dissolved earlier.
The Legislative Council can have at most one-third of the Assembly's members and not fewer than 40.
The Tamil Nadu Assembly has 235 members in the textbook, 234 elected and one nominated Anglo-Indian (additional, not in the textbook: this nominated seat was later abolished by amendment).

problem.en: Compare the Governor and the Chief Minister.

text.en: The Governor is the nominal head of the state, appointed by the President.
The Chief Minister is the real executive, with the Council of Ministers.

why.en: He holds office while he has the Assembly's majority.

text.en: The Governor acts on the aid and advice of the Council under Article 163.

prompt.en: Describe the Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council.

requiredIdeas.en: Assembly: elected, 60 to 500 members, five years
Council: at most one-third, at least 40 members
Only some states have a Council

commonMisconceptions.en: Saying every state has a Legislative Council

points.en: CM: real executive, appointed by the Governor.
Council: one-third of Assembly, minimum 40, only some states.
